Order
The award dated 24.12.2003 passed in MCC No.46/2003 by Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track Court), Betul (for short, "the Tribunal") is under challenge here,
wherein a compensation amount of Rs.3,72,200/- was awarded in favour of claimants-respondents no.1 and 2 by placing appellant under a liability to honour that award.

entities.text: Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track Court), Betul
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that deceased Anil Kumar Simaiya was the son of respondent no.3-owner of the vehicle namely Gajju Simaiya and was driving the motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-48-A-2235; pillion rider Anil Kumar Saxena was sitting on it; it was claimed that on account of failure of brakes, the motorcycle went uncontrolled and dashed against a tree on roadside; Anil Simaiya succumbed to his injuries on the way to hospital and a claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.12,92,000/- was filed by his NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9909 2 MA-2158-2004 mother and sister, who are claimants-respondents no.1 and 2 herein,
The Tribunal allowed the petition partially, both against owner Gajju Simaiya and the appellant-insurance company.

sentences.text: Appellant-insurance company had contested the claim petition on the ground that it was not liable to pay any compensation for the death of Anil Kumar Simaiya for the reason that deceased himself was responsible for the accident and under the "own damage" clause only the owner was insured.
It was also submitted that if the accident occurred on account of any mechanical failure resulting out of improper maintenance of vehicle then also the appellant-insurance company was not liable.
The claim petition was also contested on the ground that deceased was not having a valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle.

All these defence were required to be considered by the Tribunal but it confined its finding only on two aspects - first, the absence of proof on improper maintenance or mechanical failure of offending vehicle and, secondly, availability of proof regarding valid and effective driving licence of deceased on the date of accident.
It did not touch the defence raised by appellant-insurance company about not covering the risk of driver, who died on account of his own negligence.

4. In this present appeal also, the appellant-insurance company has primarily emphasized upon the fact that there was a breach of condition of insurance policy and compensation could not have been awarded for ones own negligence.
A request was accordingly made to set aside the impugned award.
5. Counsel for appellant has been heard on this appeal.
None appeared for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9909 3 MA-2158-2004 respondents.
Record of the Tribunal has been perused.

6. From the perusal of insurance policy, marked as Ex.D-5, it can be gathered that it was issued for offending motorcycle and under it, premium was taken for basic third party liability and also for basic own damage.
Since the dispute in present appeal does not involve the question regarding risk covered of a pillion rider, therefore no discussion is being made on that point.

It is clear from the terms of policy that the risk of driver of the vehicle, including the insured, was covered only under the "own damage" clause and no liability beyond that can be interpreted in terms of the policy.

The details of policy contain an elaborate discussion on personal accident cover limit for owner and driver and it provides that the total liability of insurer shall not, in aggregate, exceed the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- during any one term of insurance.
7. Now let's examine the facts of case.
Admittedly, deceased was the son of vehicle owner-respondent no.3 and he died in an accident when the vehicle driven by him dashed against a roadside tree.

In this set of facts, it is immaterial whether deceased had borrowed the motorcycle from his owner- father for one time on the date of accident or was that vehicle purchased ostensibly in the name of respondent no.3 and was in continuous possession of deceased.
The fact remains that deceased was not the owner and at the time of accident, he was driving it with the permission of his father- respondent no.3.

The borrower/the permissive user of a vehicle steps into the shoes of owner when the question of deciding the liability of insurance company comes up for interpreting his cover under the policy and such a NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9909 4 MA-2158-2004 driver can never be interpreted as a third party in relation to the vehicle in question.
Hence, by using the motorcycle as borrower/permissive user, the risk of deceased Anil Kumar Simaiya was covered only as the owner of vehicle and not as a third party.

entities.text: Man.,Bajaj Allianz Gen.Insurance ... vs Smt.Shanta Bai & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Under the scheme of compensation, the risk under "own damage" clause of an insurance policy is not covered within the ambit of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and, therefore,
respondents no.1 and 2-claimants, who had filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, were not entitled to any compensation under that provision.

For this, reliance may be placed on the judgment of Apex Court in Ningamma v. United India Insurance Company Limited,
(2009) 13 SCC 710 and New India Assurance Company Limited v. Sadanand Mukhi and others,
(2009) 2 SCC 417.
9.

sentences.text: In terms of above facts and legal principles applicable here, this appeal is allowed and appellant-insurance company is exonerated to pay any compensation decided under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act by the learned Tribunal.
The statutory amount or the compensation amount, if any, paid by appellant-insurance company shall be refunded to it.
10. Let a copy of this order along with the record of Claims Tribunal, Betul, be send back for information and necessary compliance.
